claim: llm-d has a mode that runs outside Kubernetes via a file-discovery plugin, where vLLM endpoints are listed/hardcoded rather than discovered via the Kubernetes API.
stance_target: non-Kubernetes backends are already a supported first-class deployment mode for llm-d's router
scope_conditions: practitioner walkthrough, references llm-d-router commit f7e8852479d6b2902d3bd89d8d252187211ff801
quoted_support: It's also worth mentioning that llm-d has a mode where it runs outside of k8s via a file discovery plugin, where the vLLM endpoints are hardcoded instead of discovered via the k8s API.

claim: The EPP gathers per-instance load signals by scraping each backend's Prometheus /metrics endpoint using engine-specific metric names, with a defaultEngineConfigs table mapping vllm:* and sglang:* metric names to canonical queued/running/KV-usage/LoRA/cache-info fields.
stance_target: supporting a new (non-vLLM/SGLang) backend requires only adding an engineConfigParams entry, not changing endpoint discovery
quoted_support: Name: "vllm", QueuedRequestsSpec: "vllm:num_requests_waiting", RunningRequestsSpec: "vllm:num_requests_running", KVUsageSpec: "vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc" ... Name: "sglang", QueuedRequestsSpec: "sglang:num_queue_reqs"

claim: The EPP's picker can sample endpoints according to weighted score rather than always selecting the single top-scored pod, to avoid a thundering-herd effect where traffic piles onto one 'best' replica.
stance_target: scheduler/picker design considerations relevant to any backend type
scope_conditions: llm-d-router scheduling profile: filters, scorers, picker
quoted_support: always routing to the single best pod can create a thundering herd, where everyone piles onto the same "good" replica until it stops being good. Spreading the load based on score avoids that while still favoring the better candidates

claim: For precise KV-cache tracking, the llm-d router subscribes directly to each vLLM instance's ZMQ KV-cache allocation/eviction event stream via the llm-d-kv-cache library, giving a real-time exact view of each server's KV cache at the cost of additional overhead.
stance_target: gap (c): security of EPP-to-model-server traffic outside Kubernetes includes a per-instance ZMQ event channel that a non-k8s backend must also expose
quoted_support: vLLM exposes KV-cache allocation and eviction events over ZMQ (a brokerless high-performance messaging library), and the llm-d router subscribes to these streams from every vLLM instance. This gives the router a real-time, exact view of each server's KV cache, allowing it to make precise routing decisions at the cost of a bit of additional overhead.

claim: Disaggregated prefill/decode serving transfers KV cache between nodes via RDMA (InfiniBand or RoCE), using NVIDIA's NIXL (Inference Transfer Library), bypassing the CPU.
stance_target: networking/infrastructure requirements for disaggregated serving apply regardless of orchestrator (k8s or non-k8s)
quoted_support: RDMA (remote direct memory access) moves that KV cache from prefill to decode nodes very fast, bypassing the CPU entirely. The underlying networking is InfiniBand or RoCE. llm-d uses NVIDIA's Inference Transfer Library (NIXL) for this transfer.
